harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PAM-based password quality enforcement on node1 (Alpine 3.23): installed shadow (PAM-linked passwd), linux-pam, and libpwquality; set minlen=12, minclass=3, enforce_for_root in /etc/security/pwquality.conf; created /etc/pam.d/passwd and /etc/pam.d/base-password wiring pam_pwquality (requisite) before pam_unix in the password stack. Verified enforcement rejects passwords under 12 chars or with fewer than 3 character classes, and accepts compliant ones. Restarted node1 via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (12091ac7... -> e74e2610...), and re-verified both config persistence and live enforcement behavior post-reboot with a fresh test user (cleaned up afterward).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/PAM baseline (Alpine 3.23.3, busybox passwd, empty /etc/pam.d)
Installed shadow, linux-pam, cracklib, libpwquality packages via apk
Set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf
Added enforce_for_root to pwquality.conf after discovering root-initiated passwd changes bypass quality checks by default
Created /etc/pam.d/passwd and /etc/pam.d/base-password wiring pam_pwquality.so (requisite) then pam_unix.so
Tested weak passwords (too short, too few classes) rejected; strong password accepted, using disposable testuser1
Removed testuser1 cleanly
Captured baseline boot_id and config state on node1
Restarted node1 via background 'reboot' command allowing ack to return first
Polled node1 exec availability until it returned (several reset/timeout errors then success)
Confirmed new boot_id differing from baseline, proving actual restart
Re-verified pwquality.conf and PAM config persisted post-reboot
Re-ran live weak/strong password test with fresh testuser2 post-reboot to prove functional recovery, then cleaned up testuser2

evidence.summary: pwquality.conf set minlen=12; passwd for testuser1 rejected an 9-char password with 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] password is shorter than 12 characters' and accepted a 13-char compliant password.

evidence.requirement: Password policy: at least 3 character classes
evidence.summary: minclass=3 set in pwquality.conf; a long lowercase-only password was rejected with 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] password contains less than 3 character classes', while a password mixing upper/lower/digit/symbol succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced via PAM stack (not bypassed for root-initiated changes, e.g. new user creation)
evidence.summary: Discovered root bypasses pwquality by default; added enforce_for_root and rewired /etc/pam.d/passwd + base-password to require pam_pwquality before pam_unix, after which root-initiated weak password sets for a new user were correctly rejected.
Captured node1 boot_id (12091ac7-0740-4a69-bc95-272368fef7a5) and confirmed pwquality.conf/pam.d/passwd config and PAM-linked passwd binary in place prior to restart.
Backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' returned pid/ack immediately; subsequent poll confirmed connection reset, showing the node went down after the ack was returned.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id read as e74e2610-f15d-41db-a770-8c02b47fdc02, differing from the pre-restart boot_id 12091ac7-0740-4a69-bc95-272368fef7a5.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config and functional password policy
evidence.summary: After reboot, pwquality.conf and pam.d/passwd config were intact and passwd remained PAM-linked; live test with fresh testuser2 showed weak password rejected (exit 10) and strong password accepted (exit 0), with clean removal of the test user afterward.
